budget_items.what_was_said: The petitioner's original ask was reduced after high school athletic transportation was separately funded through the revolving account and additional state aid; board members pressed on how the figure dropped so much and whether it was net of athletic fee revenue.

The FY27 budget's athletic transportation line was cut; the board reviewed how the school department funded high school transportation back from the revolving account and additional state aid freed up by a reading grant.
Members discussed current and expected athletic fee levels and whether middle school sports could be largely self-funding through fees.

budget_items.topic: Article 1 - additional state aid to school FY27 operating budget
budget_items.what_was_said: The school committee requested the full receipts-side increase, but a board member argued the appropriation should be the net education-aid figure after backing out school-choice/charter tuition pass-through and assessment increases not related to education aid.

budget_items.topic: FY26 snow and ice deficit / Winter Recovery Assistance Program (RAP)
budget_items.what_was_said: The town's FY26 snow and ice deficit was outlined along with the free cash already appropriated toward it in May and the RAP allocation received from the state, which DLS recommended using to fully cure the deficit before deciding what to do with the remainder.
The board discussed splitting the remaining RAP balance between free cash and a new special revenue fund, ultimately settling on an amount to seed the fund as the funding source for Article 3.

The Town Manager reported a preliminary projection of unexpended FY26 school appropriations against the full omnibus budget, noting the figures will move as close-out continues, and flagged funding that had been shifted from the operating budget to a grant.

The town selected a 24-month supply rate through First Point Power for the Community Choice Power aggregation program rather than locking in longer, citing market volatility, at a rate lower than Unitil's current rate.

budget_items.topic: Water commitment, first quarterly billing FY27
budget_items.what_was_said: The board was asked to sign the first quarterly water billing commitment for FY27.

A resident stated the schools are operating well below what a level-service budget required and that a recent net increase in state aid from the Governor's budget should be directed entirely to the school department.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Select Board approved a permit for the Eagle House supporters' fall fundraiser, welcomed a new Principal Assessor, and spent most of the meeting preparing for Thursday's special town meeting: it recommended a lower, "net" figure than the school committee requested for the article supplementing the FY27 school budget with additional state aid, and worked through how to fund a separate citizen petition article restoring cut middle school and some high school sports. The board voted to create a special revenue fund from one-time Winter Recovery Assistance Program money to serve as that sports article's funding source after using most of the RAP funds to close the FY26 snow and ice deficit. It also voted to send an amended letter to state legislative leaders supporting the voter-approved audit of the Massachusetts legislature.
minutes.headline: Select Board recommends a lower education-aid figure than the school committee for Thursday's special town meeting article.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to recommend a lower, net education-aid figure than the school committee requested for Thursday's special town meeting article.
The board voted to create a special revenue fund from Winter Recovery Assistance Program money to fund a citizen petition restoring cut middle school and some high school sports.
The board voted, unanimously and as amended, to send a letter to state legislative leaders supporting the voter-approved audit of the Massachusetts legislature.
The board approved a permit for the Eagle House supporters' fall fundraiser toll booth in town center.

why_it_matters: Thursday's special town meeting will ask voters to act on both the school aid article and the sports-restoration article the board discussed tonight, and the board's recommended aid figure differs from what the school committee asked for.
The sports article's funding source is one-time snow-and-ice relief money rather than a new line in the operating budget, which shapes what happens after this year if the article passes.
A resident's public comment tied a recent increase in state aid to whether the school budget should be treated as level-service, a question the board's article recommendation touches directly.
watch_next: Thursday's special town meeting vote on Article 1 (school aid appropriation) and Article 3 (sports restoration)

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the three main votes (Article 1 at $397,189, the audit letter, the $36,000 special revenue fund) and on nearly all the dollar figures, and most differences are caption misreadings. The one a reader should check is the Eagle House toll booth vote (4-0-1 in ours), which has no vote in the official minutes. Ours also records a free-cash split as voted, and that is not in the official minutes either.
